## FA-009 / ZEUS-49fb81e7348d revision 1 — Refs #10

### Defect (upstream, agreed in cross-review)
Upstream suites confused wiring-string checks with behavior: `test_context_programming_smoke.py` verifies the l2_driver wiring by `code_only` substring presence; `test_entrance_reconfirm_contract.py` duplicates the verdict formula locally and asserts AST intersection without executing apply/ledger; `test_curator_smoke.py` encodes the defect as its expectation. The review's own isolated PASS of those suites explicitly "does not resolve the limitation of string wiring checks". Consensus: assets are API/behavior tests with positive and negative controls; string presence is never inherited as an E2E PASS.

### Zeus
A sweep of the suite found no test asserting on production source substrings; the only source-reading tests are the structural policy tests in `test_architecture.py`. This PR turns that state into a guard:
- `tests/test_architecture.py`: `wiring_assertions(source)` flags `assert` expressions that read production source text/bytes/AST (`src/`, `scripts/`, `harness_hooks/`, `codex_harness.`); `test_tests_assert_behavior_not_source_text` applies it to every `tests/test_*.py` (allowlist: the structural policy module); `test_wiring_detector_has_positive_and_negative_controls` pins 3 positive and 5 negative examples (runtime files, executed results, observed outputs, reads outside assert, parsed values).
- `docs/contracts.md`: `INV-RESEARCH-003` sentence; `docs/zeus/implementation/behavior-assertions-001/README.md`.

### Verification
| | Result |
|---|---|
| `tests/test_architecture.py` (guard + controls) | 4 passed; 0 offenders in the current suite |
| Windows full `uv run pytest -q` (Python 3.12.14) / `ruff check` | 919 passed, 305 skipped / clean |
| Linux path | this PR's ubuntu CI matrix |

### Not claimed
The detector is a heuristic over `assert` expressions that read source directly; a read stored in a variable and asserted later is not caught and remains a review rule. Upstream tests are not modified (ticket scope is this repository); their PASS is simply not inherited. Issue closure follows the ledger acceptance path (#30) and is a separate step after this PR; the GitHub issue stays OPEN until that acceptance.
